answer: Escrowed Reputation Drawdown. Each identity posts a refundable deposit plus a small nonrefundable lagoon fee at registration; the deposit is released only after 90 days of upheld transactions. Any upheld fraud complaint drains the accused's deposit to compensate the victim before the attacker can withdraw. Cloning N identities costs N nonrefundable fees plus N locked deposits, while an honest agent risks only one. A jetty of escrow holds funds against disputes, and a zephyr of refundable release keeps honest capital cheap.
